title: Setup command
responsibility: Compose the whole first run in one ordered, resumable, idempotent command over the existing primitives: resolve and print every path before mutating, validate the runtime, take the setup lock, install the locked dependencies as a bootstrap mutation confined to the .planning checkout, then plan the transaction, run the existing initializer under it, establish state protection, install and register the package, obtain each consent in its own step, bind and prove the model, read back everything it wrote, and either launch the combined runtime or explain exactly what remains. Use a distinct exit code per refusal class and publish the mapping.
notes: ⚠️ ITS PRE-INSTALL IMPORT GRAPH IS BUILT-INS ONLY. Setup runs before the dependency graph it installs exists, so a top-level import of Pi, Ajv or anything else installed is not a style question — the command cannot start. Everything after the install step is loaded dynamically. ⚠️ IT IS NOT A SECOND INITIALIZER: `bin/init-project.mjs` keeps its content-only contract and its refusal semantics. ⚠️ THE INSTALL COMES BEFORE THE TRANSACTION PLAN (D26, 2026-09-22). The dependency install comes before the transaction plan because the plan validates existing Kiln records, and that validation needs Ajv, which the install is what provides. Everything up to and including the install is therefore built-ins only (ACC-0083), and the install is a bootstrap mutation confined to the .planning checkout: it changes no consumer project state and does not rewrite the lockfile. An interruption during the bootstrap has no journal to resume from, and must leave consumer project state unchanged.
